dedupe_keys.name: adcirc circulation and storm surge model

description: ADCIRC is a finite-element model of time-dependent free-surface circulation and transport developed by the ADCIRC university and government research community. It represents two- and three-dimensional domains on unstructured meshes for storm surge, flooding, tides and nearshore operations. Inputs define the mesh and hydraulic forcing; outputs describe simulated circulation and water levels, with optional netCDF output. Geographic extent and time steps are selected for each application, not fixed to a single coast or historical period. Source is free under LGPL-3.0-or-later and uses Fortran and C, with optional MPI libraries. A limitation is that users must match test examples to the code version while documentation is being consolidated across several sites. ADCIRC can supply coastal hazard conditions for infrastructure exposure and resilience simulations. TELEMAC-MASCARET (model-telemac-mascaret) provides related hydrodynamic modelling. The repository shows real coastal applications, but those images alone do not establish independently reusable case-study packages.
